findings.q: Can the 207 missing bedroom counts be filled in safely?
findings.a: Yes. Missingness shows no relation to other variables, and a k-NN imputer recovers hidden values with an error of 59 rooms against 420 for the median. The effect on price prediction is negligible.

findings.q: How strongly does income drive house value?
findings.a: Strongly: correlation 0.69. Every extra $10,000 of district income goes with about $41,736 more in house value, though income alone explains only 47 % of the variation.

A great deal. Ocean proximity has a large effect and prices are strongly clustered in space (Moran's I = 0.79). Adding distances to five major cities cut error by 3.0 % for a linear model and 1.7 % for gradient boosting.
Yes, modestly and consistently: rooms, bedrooms and people per household cut error by 1.5 % to 2.7 %, and every comparison was statistically significant.
XGBoost, with a test error (RMSE) of $40,980 and R² of 0.87. It beats the runner-up, HistGB, by a small but statistically reliable margin.
On the most expensive districts. Values are capped at $500,001 in the data; those districts are 4.3 % of the test set but cause 16 % of the squared error.
